title: The child becoming quiet
note: Fictional patient. Doses and energies are quoted from the 2025 AHA guidelines (and the ERC where named) for recognition; your unit protocol, crash-cart stock and the attending nephrologist come first. Simulation success is an educational result, not a prediction of patient survival.
intro: Jun-Jun, 8, 22 kg, arrived coughing and breathing fast after gaining 1.8 kg. Forty minutes into dialysis he is drowsy and pale, with slow shallow breaths. Saturation 82%; heart rate 54 (it was 120). You are the pediatric dialysis nurse.

n1.prompt: What is happening, and what is first?

choices.text: Respiratory failure with hypoxic bradycardia: call for help and the pediatric cart; open the airway; bag-mask ventilation with oxygen using the right mask size.
choices.feedback: In children, breathing usually fails first; ventilation breaks the chain.

choices.text: Atropine for the slow heart rate.
choices.feedback: Hypoxic bradycardia needs oxygen and ventilation, not atropine.
With a pulse and a rate over 60 for now, effective ventilation comes first.
choices.then: A colleague takes the airway and ventilates; the rate rises.

n2.scene: With bagging, saturation 90%, heart rate 88. The physician-on-duty and attending pediatric nephrologist are called.

choices.text: Report the fluid status and pressure; the physicians decide whether fluid removal continues for the edema or stops for pressure.
choices.feedback: In pulmonary edema, fluid removal may be treatment; it is a physician decision.

choices.text: Stop fluid removal automatically because he is unwell.
choices.feedback: Stopping may remove part of the treatment for edema; ask the physician.

n3.scene: Despite good bag-mask ventilation with oxygen, his heart rate falls to 50 and he is mottled with weak pulses.

choices.text: Start pediatric CPR: one-third chest depth, 100 to 120 a minute, 15:2 with two rescuers; epinephrine by weight if compromise persists after hypoxia is corrected.
choices.feedback: PALS 2025: CPR for HR under 60 with compromise despite effective oxygenated ventilation (COR 1).

choices.text: Wait until the heart rate is under 40.
choices.feedback: The threshold is under 60 with poor perfusion despite ventilation.

end.title: 3:15 p.m.
end.text: Jun-Jun’s heart rate recovers with ventilation and brief CPR; he is moved to the pediatric intensive care unit with a plan for gentle fluid removal there.

debrief:
What this case teaches

  • Breathing fails first in children; ventilate with the right mask.
  • Under 60 with poor perfusion despite ventilation: compressions.
  • The circuit decision belongs to the physicians.
